body.title: Integration-test the I/O wrapper against a temp INSRC home
body.summary: Add src/config/__tests__/config-reconcile-io.test.ts extending the on-disk fixture idiom already used at src/config/__tests__/repo-shaper-override.test.ts:27 (materialise a config file → run the code under test → assert on the resulting file). Use a temp INSRC home per test and a write-counting fs seam that counts writeFile invocations targeting the config document (temp or final) plus rename invocations, so 'written at most once' is an assertion rather than an inference — this is what fences off any N-round-trip implementation, including one that writes the temp file twice. Cover: the t2 legacy fixture producing exactly 1 writeFile + 1 rename with the three dynamic namespaces byte-identical; an already-normalized config producing 0 writeFile and 0 rename and an unchanged mtime; ENOENT first-boot equivalence; unreadable file (EACCES/EISDIR, skip-guarded when running as root); corrupt/truncated/zero-byte JSON aborting with no write and explicitly asserting no default-fill fallback; write failure leaving no temp file behind; concurrent modification abandoning the write; a ConfigCatalogError surfacing as its own outcome kind; and path resolution going through PATHS.config.
acceptanceChecks: Every listed integration subject has a test and the suite passes under `npx tsx --test 'src/config/__tests__/*.test.ts'`

The write-counting seam counts writeFile invocations targeting the config document (temp or final) and rename invocations, and asserts exactly 1 of each for the legacy fixture and exactly 0 of each for the already-normalized case, with mtime asserted unchanged in the latter
The corrupt-JSON test asserts the on-disk bytes are identical after the run and that the dynamic namespaces were not default-filled over
A catalog-integrity failure is asserted to surface as a distinct outcome kind from an I/O or parse failure
Permission-based tests skip cleanly rather than fail when the suite runs as root
Tests add no new package dependency

tests.name: legacy config on disk → exactly 1 writeFile + 1 rename, resulting document normalized, dynamic namespaces byte-identical
already-normalized config → zero writeFile, zero rename, mtime unchanged (steady state)
ENOENT → degrades to reconcileConfig(undefined) and writes defaults once (first-boot equivalence)
unreadable file (EACCES/EISDIR, root-skip-guarded) → nothing written, existing file untouched, errno surfaced
corrupt / truncated / zero-byte JSON → aborts writing nothing, reports parse message + byte offset, on-disk bytes identical and no default-fill fallback
write failure (ENOSPC/EACCES) → temp file unlinked, no partial or half-renamed document, counts reported alongside the error
concurrent modification between read stat and pre-rename re-stat → write abandoned, newer document intact, non-fatal outcome recorded
ConfigCatalogError surfaces as a structurally distinct outcome kind from I/O and parse failures
path resolution goes through PATHS.config against a temp INSRC home; no hardcoded ~/.insrc path is exercised
